stem: Pranav looks at the diagram. Straight lines $\ell$ and $m$ lie on the same flat page and meet at point $P$. The angles at $P$ are labelled $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly names the lines and the angle structure at $P$?

options.text: Lines $\ell$ and $m$ are intersecting, and their meeting at $P$ forms the four angles labelled $1$ to $4$.
Lines $\ell$ and $m$ can meet at two different points on the page if they are drawn longer.
The four angles at $P$ are what force lines $\ell$ and $m$ to meet.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: On one flat page, two straight lines that meet at a single point are intersecting, and that meeting forms four angles.

teacher.key_rationale: Intersecting coplanar lines meet at one point and form four angles. Claiming a second meeting point, or saying the angles cause the meeting, leaves that structure.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as coplanar lines l and m meeting at P with four labelled angles.
